data.narrative:
Specter is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Xerxes Libsch and Philip Clark that has raised $6.8M to date. The relevant comp universe comprises one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI, though the broader robotics sector contains ten same-sector companies overall.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach, using the $6.8M raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement in this sector. This yields an implied valuation of $17M. The peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints: while ten robotics peers exist in the dataset, only one operated at the same stage, with zero in adjacent stages or similar valuation tiers—below the minimum threshold of three required for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $14M to $20M, centered on $17M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty around the stage-progression multiplier itself, which assumes Specter's trajectory mirrors typical seed advancement patterns. Key unknowns affecting any future revaluation include product-market validation metrics, capital efficiency, and competitive positioning within the robotics manufacturing subsector. A broader peer dataset at comparable stages would strengthen conviction in this range.
